# Introduction

The isolved API is intended to provide a clean and modern interface for third party applications to integrate with the isolved suite of applications.   This new API is implemented as a representational state transfer (REST) interface that runs over HTTPS.

The API is secured using the OAuth 2.0 protocol and requires the use of bearer tokens to access resources.  Details on the OAuth 2.0 specification can be found here: 

http://oauth.net/2/

OAuth defines a number of “flows” that describe different usage scenarios for client applications to communicate with server resources.  The isolved API makes use of two of these flows: Client Credentials and Resource Owner Password Credentials.  These two flow types cover the usage scenarios that the API was intended to initially be used for and will likely be expanded on in future releases.  

An abbreviated and very well organized summary of how OAuth 2 flows work can also be found here:

https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/an-introduction-to-oauth-2

# Authentication

In order for a third party application to be able to access the API it must first request a token.  The token request will always be the initial step that needs to be performed before any subsequent calls to other resources within the API may be requested.   In many OAuth 2 server implementations the authorization server is separated from the API server but in the case of isolved, for simplicity, the authorization server and API server are one and the same.  Note that this could change in a future version.

Applications that intend to make use of the isolved API must be registered within the isolved web application as an “API Application”.  Once the API Application entry is created an OAuth Client ID and secret key values are generated and are used to request tokens within the API. 

To request a token the third party application must make a POST request to the API authorization server.  The OAuth Client ID and secret obtained from within the isolved API application registration must be passed in the HTTP Authorization header for the request using basic authentication.

The Authorization header is constructed as follows:

1.	The client_id and secret are combined into a string separated by a colon `client_id:secret`.
2.	The resulting string is then encoded using the RFC2045-MIME variant of Base64, except not limited to 74 characters per line.
3.	The authorization method and a space (ie. “Basic”) is then put before the encoded string.

For example: 

`Authorization: Basic [REDACTED_DOCUMENTATION_CREDENTIAL]`

The following is a successful response sample for a token:

```
{
    "access_token": "[REDACTED_DOCUMENTATION_TOKEN]",
    "token_type": "bearer",
    "expires_in": 300,
    "refresh_token": "[REDACTED_DOCUMENTATION_TOKEN]"
}
```

The access token is provided in the 'access_token' property, along with the 'token_type'.  This bearer token type must be specified in the Authorization header of subsequent requests to the API along with the `access_token` value.  (See below)

The `expires_in` specifies the number of seconds before the access token is expired and a new one must be requested.  Typical access token lifetimes are 5 minutes.

The `refresh_token` value is a secondary token that can be used to obtain a new access token without having to present isolved user credentials in a new token request.  The `refresh_token` value is presented in token request using the grant_type value of 'refresh_token'.  (See below)

Refresh token lifetimes are typlically valid for 30 days on the same device it was generated from.  (Note: A refresh token may be invalidated by an admistrator.)

## Resource Owner Password Flow

In the Resource Owner Password flow, the client application collects the end user (resource owner) credentials on behalf of the isolved application.   The username, password and optional client code can be collected within the third party application and are passed to the authorization server in the token request. 

These values are passed in the body of the request encoded using the `x-www-form-urlencoded` format.  In this format each value is in the format `name=value` and separated from other values with an `&` symbol.

Note: As of isolved version 6.5, the authorization header for the password flow token request no longer requires the API application secret to be passed. Only the client_id value is required.

For example:

```
POST /api/token HTTP/1.1

grant_type=password&username=user&password=password&clientCode=1234
```

### Multi-Factor Authentication Enabled Scenarios

When requesting an access token for an isolved user using the password grant type/flow, the user must authenticate using a secondary authentication scheme to validate that the user signing in is not being impersonated.  This is the same process that exists within the isolved web user interface.  In some cases based on company or system policies the multi-factor authentication may be bypassed.  If multi-factor authentication is required, the response from the token request will be as follows:

```
403 FORBIDDEN:

{
    "reason": "mfa_required",
    "mfaEmailRoute": "{email_url}",
    "mfaSMSRoute": "{sms_url}",
    "mfaMethod": "POST",
    "emailMask": "####@isolvedhcm.com",
    "smsMask": "###-###-1234",
    "mfaToken": "{mfa_token}",
    "mfaRouteExpiration": "2020-01-24T23:09:20.3277469Z"
}
```

A status code of '403 FORBIDDEN' will be returned and the following data elements will indicate next steps and actions that can be performed.  

The `mfaEmailRoute` parameter will contain a URL endpoint within the API, which if the end user chooses to deliver their authorization code via email, will initiate the process of generating a new code and delivering the email to their email address on file.
The client application can display the masked email address as visual confirmation that the email address is correct before choosing that path.

The `mfaSMSRoute`, if non-null, will contain a URL endpoint which if the user chooses to deliver their authorization code via SMS text, will initiate sending the text to the user's confiugured mobile phone number.
The client application can display the masked SMS number provided in `smsMask` to confirm the last four digits of their mobile phone number before choosing that path.  Note that if the SMS properties described here are `null`, then the SMS option is not available for the given user.

The `mfaMethod` parameter indicates which HTTP method to use when requesting the delivery via the URL's provided.

The `mfaToken` is a special access token designed to only be used for multi-factor authentication.  The token has an expiration in which it must be used. 

Finally the `mfaRouteExpiration` indicates the absolute date and time (UTC) in which the MFA process must be completed.

### Multi-Factor Access Code Delivery & Acceptance

Once requested using the `mfaEmailRoute` or `mfaSMSRoute`, the access code delivery cannot be requested again.  The client application must complete this special MFA flow using the `mfa_token` originally received and can only be used once.

After the user has received their authentication code via one of the delivery methods provided, the client application must collect the access code as input.  This code must then be re-sent to a new token request using the `password` grant_type by appending the following two new parameters in the body of the request:

`mfa_token` - The MFA token provided in the original token request's forbidden response must be sent as validation and must no be expired.

`mfa_authCode` - The MFA access code the user provided as input.

If the access code provided is incorrect or the MFA token has expired, a new MFA process will be initiated and the `403 FORBIDDEN` response will be returned.  

If the access code provided matches the delivered code, a standard access_token response will be recieved.

* NOTE - The MFA process will be required for all `password` grant types. It is highly recommended that clients also implement the use of refresh tokens along with MFA.  Requests for access_tokens using a refresh token do not require multi-factor authentication.


## Client Credential Flow

In the client credentials flow, the third party application calling into the API does not have any isolved user context.  The call may even be made without any direct user intervention.  In this case access to the isolved application is determined by the role and default user configuration assigned to the API Application entry within isolved.   

Obtaining a token using the client credentials flow is the same as that of the password grant type, except that the `grant_type` requested changes to `client_credentials` and the username, password and clientCode form values are omitted.

## Refresh Token Flow

Refresh tokens allow requesting a new access token without re-presenting all the isolved user credentials.  This allows clients running on end user machines to not have to permanently store user credentials to maintain access to the isolved REST API.  

When an access token has expired and a refresh token is available, the client can request a new access token specifying the `refresh_token` grant type and providing the refresh token in the `refresh_token` form parameter.  As in the other token request flows, the parameters are `x-www-form-urlencoded`.  Below is an example token request payload containing a refresh token:

```
POST /api/token HTTP/1.1

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={refresh_token}
```
**New in Release 6.6**:  Refresh tokens can optionally include an `ess_employee_id` parameter to request that a different self-service employee can be requested for the new access token.  The employee Id specified must be associated with the original user that generated the refresh token and can only be used by self-service employee user types.  

```
POST /api/token HTTP/1.1

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={refresh_token}&ess_employee_id={ess_employee_id}
```
The specified ess_employee_id value must be numeric and match to an existing self-service employee record.  These Id's can be obtained once authenticated via the API for the first time and using any of the **employee list** or **userInfo** API's.

*Note that when requesting a new access token using a refresh token scoped to one employee but requesting a different employee associated with the same user, a new refresh token value will be generated.*


## Making Authenticated Requests

To authenticate subsequent API requests, you must provide a valid bearer token in an HTTP header:

`Authorization: Bearer {bearer_token}`

## Self Service Employee Scope

When authenticated as an isolved self-service employee the desired self-service scope can be indicated on **any** API call by adding the `essScope` parameter to the query string of the request:

```
?essScope={Employee|Manager|Supervisor|All*}
```

\* The `All` scope is a specialized option that is only supported on the `userInfo` API call.  In all other cases, this would be automatically interpreted as `Employee`.

# Paginated Results

Some of the calls within this API return a paged result set.  This means that the results of the API call may not contain every item has been located based on the filters provided.   Paged results are used by API’s that may potentially return very large result sets.   

Paged results have a default page size of 50.  When calling a paged API the result will always be wrapped with a header that looks like the following:

```
{
  "totalPages": 1,
  "totalItems": 1,
  "previousPageUrl": null,
  "nextPageUrl": null,
  "results": [...]
}
```

Where the total number page pages in the paged result is specified in the `totalPages` attribute.  The total number of items are specified in the `totalItems` attribute.  

Navigation between pages is achieved by making a subsequent call to the api and specifying the `page` argument on the query string:

`/api/clients/{client_id}/legals/{legal_id}/employees?page=1'

In the above call the `page` argument indicates that page number 1 is requested.  Pages are zero-based, so page #1 is the second logical page of results, or items 51-100.

To assist in navigating through the result sets dynamically the paged data set header also includes a `nextPageUrl` and `previousPageUrl` attributes that will supply the full URL needed to pull the next and previous page of data.  If there are no previous or next pages to display (such as when at the beginning or end of a large data set, or when there is only one page) then these attributes will be null, respectively.

The paged portion of results that were requested are contained in the `results` list of the paged header.

# Versioning

While every effort will be made between releases to provide full backward compatibility in API updates there are times when a breaking change is unavoidable.  When this happens we will version off a specific API endpoint so that it will always continue to function in the same way it originally was written.  New or breaking functionality will be provided in another version that must be explicitly requested.  In order to do this a specific HTTP header must be present when making requests to API's that support multiple versions:

`X-API-VERSION: {version number}`

If this header value is not specified the lowest available version is automatically selected.

post.description:
Hires a new employee into the specified client within iSolved.

Resident Location logic:

Automatic Selection:
- The API uses the zip code and city name from the request payload to identify the correct tax location.
- If a zip code returns multiple tax locations and one of those locations has a city name that matches the employee's city value in the payload, that location is automatically selected.
- The 'useDefaultGeoCode' query parameter: When true allows the first geocode in the list to be selected automatically.

Manual Selection Required:
- If the API cannot determine the resident location the API will respond with a list of available tax location options. The user must then select the appropriate location from the provided list.

laborGroups.description:
List of eligible Labor Groups
The following describes the meaning of each type of value returned:

1. LaborGroups = null - The rule set entry is available to all client labor groups.  
   This will occur when the rule set entry does not have any "Punch Matches Labor Field" conditions assigned.
2. LaborGroups = [] -  If the value returns an empty array, the rule set entry has at least one 
   "Punch Matches Labor Field" condition assigned and no client labor group matches the condition(s).
3. LaborGroups = [{LaborGroupId, LaborGroupName, LaborFieldIds=[n,n,...]}, x, x,...] - If the value returns a populated array of client labor groups, the rule set entry has at least one 
   "Punch Matches Labor Field" condition assigned and the client labor groups in the array match the condition(s).
